title: Capstone — The Mastery Scorecard
subtitle: Fresh clone to defended scorecard: run the whole discipline end-to-end and prove, with graded numbers, that you now excel at context engineering
topics: The end-to-end run — seed → gates → app → full graded campaign → scorecard
The headline metric — tokens ↓ at 100% key-fact correctness (never tokens alone)
Seam failures — where stages meet is where systems actually break
The six-competency self-checklist — 'you now excel when…'
Competency built: ALL SIX — this module is the exam

analogy.title: Opening Night at the Restaurant You Built
analogy.text: Culinary school ends the same way every discipline does: not with a quiz about knives, but with a service — you plan the menu, stock the walk-in, run the line, and serve real covers while the instructors watch the pass. Nobody asks whether you can julienne; they watch whether the fish course arrives correct, on time, and costed. U14 is your service: a fresh clone of MedFlow, every gate run in order, a full graded campaign, and a one-page scorecard you can defend line by line — where every line says both what it cost AND whether it was right.

antiPatterns: The scorecard with one column — tokens without verdicts is a menu without allergen labels
Skipping the gates because 'nothing changed' — the capstone grade is for the protocol, not the luck
Explaining a seam failure away instead of writing it down — the seams section is the most reread part of any postmortem

sections.title: 🔬 On the bench
sections.body:
Do: Everything: fresh clone → seed gate → grader selftest → app tests → full campaign → reconcile → route.

See: The bench is the exam. scorecard.py refuses to render past a broken gate — pass it and the six-competency rubric is yours with evidence attached.

Bench not running? App guide · SETUP.md

sections.title: The Run
sections.body:
The capstone is a protocol, executed on a fresh clone, in order — each step gated by the one before it:

1. Contract: python bench/keys/generate_keys.py — the seed must verify (10 determinations) before anything downstream is trusted. 2. Grader: python bench/verify_selftest.py — prove the instrument can fail (it must catch the planted wrong answer AND the planted fabrication). 3. App: backend tests green (./mvnw test — golden determinations, per-mode reconciliation, abstention, fidelity), then boot both halves in replay mode. 4. Campaign: python bench/run_campaign.py --modes all ten --replay — 100 graded cells. 5. Reconcile: your U13 reconciler — zero layer drift, zero instrument disagreements. 6. Route: your U12 derivation — the table must re-derive from THIS run's grid, not the shipped one. Only then do you write the scorecard.

sections.title: The Scorecard
sections.body:
One page, five defended lines, every number from YOUR run's results/ (the shipped reference: routed 239 median tokens vs naive 1,696 — 7.1x at 100% correctness; okf 9.1x on canonical; abstention correct on both traps at 157 tokens; two disclosed teaching failures, naive×Q7 and compressed×Q9, both caught):

Line 1 — Tokens: routed vs naive median, with the source label (synthetic-pre-recording or live). Line 2 — Correctness: per-arm percentages, FAILs named, savings-void cells listed. Line 3 — Truth: abstention verdicts on Q7/Q8 and the fidelity assertion's status. Line 4 — Freshness: gate outputs with timestamps — when did the contract last verify. Line 5 — Provenance: which quantity (U13) every headline number is, stated plainly. A scorecard whose every line survives the question 'how do you know?' is the course outcome made visible.

sections.title: Seam Failures — Where It Actually Breaks
sections.body: The kit's M31 closed on the observation that production failures live at the SEAMS between stages, not within them — and this course's own build history is the evidence. The response-shape seam: harness expecting flat JSON, backend wrapping in primary — 100 cells of zeros, caught only because 0-token PASSes are impossible. The instrument seam: a benchmark's graph arm running against a silently-crashed server for two whole campaigns. The derivation seam: UI mirrors hand-copied from the seed, one edit away from U11's silent rot. Your capstone writeup must include a seams section: at least two places where YOUR run's stages meet and could fail without an error — and what mechanical check now guards each. Finding none doesn't mean there are none; it means your run hasn't failed yet.

sections.title: You Now Excel When…
sections.body:
The six-competency rubric, self-graded with evidence from your run:

① Diagnose: given any receipt, you can name the dominant layer and the strategy family that attacks it. ② Four strategies: you can classify all ten modes into write/select/compress/isolate — and explain the two that resist the taxonomy. ③ Static surface: you can state why cached mode's CLEAN prefix hits and what edit would silently zero it. ④ Long horizons: you can say which of compaction/notes/isolation fits a given task shape, and what isolated's 1,805-token single-question price buys. ⑤ Govern truth: you can show a fabrication being caught by shape, and staleness being caught by a gate, within a day. ⑥ Measure: you can put any published number in its quantity class and say what would make it comparable to yours. Six boxes, each with a pointer into your own results — that is what 'excelling at context engineering' means here, and nothing less counts.

sections.question: Your capstone run reports routed at 8.9x over naive — better than the shipped 7.1x reference — and a reviewer asks you to defend the improvement. WHICH defense demonstrates course mastery?
options: A. 'Higher is better; the course reference was conservative'

B. 'Both are replay-quantity numbers; my delta traces to re-derived routes after I fixed compressed's Q9 fidelity — here is the re-graded grid showing compressed now eligible for aggregations at 100%, the reconciler's zero-disagreement output, and the freshness gate run after my change'
C. 'The number came from run_campaign.py, which the course itself ships, so it is correct by construction'
D. 'I averaged three replay runs to reduce variance'
sections.explanation: B walks all six competencies in one answer: quantity class named (U13), the causal change attributed (U11's drift attribution), correctness re-verified per class (U12's route-only-among-correct), instruments reconciled, gates rerun. A celebrates without provenance; C confuses the instrument with the verdict (tools are trusted because they can fail, not because they shipped); D reveals a misunderstanding — replay is deterministic, so averaging it is theater, which a master would know.

sections.title: Capstone Theater
items: The reference-number capstone: quoting the shipped grid instead of running your own — the protocol IS the exam; the numbers are just its receipt.
Green-path-only writeups: no seams section, no FAILs mentioned — a report that can't name where it would break is a demo, and this course has spent fourteen modules on the difference.
Rubric self-grading without pointers: six checked boxes and zero file paths — evidence-free mastery is the anecdote trap wearing a graduation gown.

sections.title: Sources
sections.body: Sources: everything — [ANTHROPIC-CE] (anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents), [LC-WSCI] (langchain.com/blog/context-engineering-for-agents), [ROT-LIT], [SG-GUIDE], and both parent courses [PARENT-KIT]/[PARENT-KG] — full references in docs/canon.md.

takeaway: Mastery is a protocol you can rerun and a scorecard you can defend: gates before trust, correctness gating every token number, seams named before they fail, and each of the six competencies backed by a pointer into results you produced yourself.
labUnderstand: Dry-run the protocol against the shipped artifacts: execute steps 1–2 (contract gate, grader selftest) for real, trace steps 3–6 through the existing results files, and draft your seams section — two seam risks with the mechanical check that guards each.
labBuild: With Claude, build scorecard.py: run the full protocol on your clone (gates → campaign → reconcile → route derivation) and emit the five-line scorecard plus the six-competency rubric with evidence pointers — then break one gate on purpose and confirm the scorecard refuses to render.
